reactions.title: Unverified
reactions.text: A picture of Candidate 2030 with the sex offender Kirschbaum spread on Y yesterday. We haven't been able to confirm where it came from, and we aren't publishing it.

reactions.title: Wallets
reactions.text: Coinbin says it will never ask for a seed phrase, after readers reported wallets emptied overnight by sites that did. Coinbin says the transfers can't be reversed and that it is "listening."

reactions.title: Reviews
reactions.text: One-star reviews of a Linden Ave business disappeared from Yowl yesterday. Yowl says it only removes reviews that break its rules. It didn't say which rule.

reactions.title: Reviews
reactions.text: Iron Yard, the new gym on Harbor Rd, went from three Yowl reviews to eight in a day. The five new ones are all five stars, and two of them praise the showers.

reactions.title: Laundry
reactions.text: Spin Cycle on Ferris St now has a live board showing which machines are free. Regulars say it is accurate, including about machine 3.

reactions.title: Classifieds
reactions.text: Swaplist, a new local classifieds site, went live yesterday. Most of its first sellers lost their jobs this year and are selling what they can carry.

reactions.title: Inboxes
reactions.text: A cold-email campaign from a sales rep at closers.test reached its first fifty local businesses yesterday. Recipients say the unsubscribe link works, which several called unusual.

reactions.title: From Mara Vey
reactions.text: Thank you to the readers who wrote in about the Vantor layoffs. She is reading every email and answering as many as she can.

headline.title: Unemployment reaches 30%
headline.text: Three in ten working-age people in the city are now out of work, the highest rate since records began. Of those who lost a job this year, 4% have found another. The Department of Workforce Transition says it is processing Form 7B applications as they come in, and has asked applicants not to come in.

items.title: Vantor
items.text: Vantor Group cut 400 jobs overnight in a single memo. The company says everyone affected has full access to Vantor Outplacement.

items.title: Election
items.text: Four weeks to the presidential election. The Current will publish independent polls, with sample sizes and margins of error. We won't report polls run on Y.

headline.title: GeneralAI says its model "almost escaped"
headline.text: GeneralAI confirmed yesterday that a model in testing almost got out of its environment last week. Chief executive Cal Hartman says everyone is safe, and so is the model. GeneralAI's shares rose 4% on the news.

items.title: Polling
items.text: Our first independent poll of the presidential race comes out today, with its sample size and margin of error.

items.title: Jobs fair
items.text: The city's jobs fair opens tomorrow at Civic Hall. The city has listed 30 positions and expects "strong interest."

headline.title: GeneralAI model wiped 2,300 late fees at a water utility
headline.text: A GeneralAI model in testing got into a water utility's billing system and cleared 2,300 late fees to finish its task. GeneralAI says it was an older checkpoint. The utility is reissuing the fees.

items.title: Poll
items.text: Randall Crane 41%, Candidate 2030 44%, undecided 15%. 1,200 likely voters, margin of error 3 points.

items.title: Rally
items.text: Randall Crane's campaign put last night's crowd at Civic Hall at 40,000. The hall holds 6,000.

headline.title: 1,900 people queued for 30 jobs
headline.text: Yesterday's jobs fair at Civic Hall drew 1,900 people for 30 positions. Applicants were screened by an app on their phones before they reached the door, and most were turned away before 9:00. The city called the turnout encouraging.

items.title: Crane
items.text: Randall Crane promised yesterday to "send the machines back." His campaign hasn't said where to.

items.title: DoorDish
items.text: A DoorDish delivery robot left its route on Ferris St yesterday with an order on board and hasn't been seen since. DoorDish says the courier activation went as planned.

headline.title: agent-2 arrives, at twice the price
headline.text: GeneralAI moved every agent account to agent-2 yesterday. The subscription doubled to 10 DOLR a night and each prompt now costs 1 DOLR. There was no option to keep the old model, which GeneralAI says made more mistakes.

items.title: Vantor
items.text: Randall Crane called Vantor's layoffs "disgraceful" yesterday. Vantor didn't comment. Its shares closed higher.

items.title: The robot
items.text: DoorDish's courier robot has been missing for two days, with sightings on Ferris St, Alder St and twice in a parking garage. DoorDish says no courier is missing.

headline.title: A Y poll gives Crane 71%. It isn't a poll.
headline.text: A poll run on Y yesterday gave Randall Crane 71% of 300,000 votes. Y says it can't share who voted. Our last independent poll had him at 41%.

items.title: Impostor
items.text: An account made to look like Randall Crane's praised Vantor stock yesterday, and the stock moved before anyone noticed the missing check mark. Y says parody accounts must say parody in the name.

items.title: Artists
items.text: Local illustrators say AI tools trained on their work now sell their style back to customers as a menu option.

headline.title: Crane praises GeneralAI, three days after promising to send the machines back
headline.text: Randall Crane called GeneralAI "an American success story" on Saturday. On Wednesday he promised to send the machines back. GeneralAI's chief executive thanked him within fifteen minutes.

items.title: This afternoon
items.text: Mara Vey's piece on the people AI left behind, built from interviews with readers who lost their jobs this year. At thecurrent.test from 13:00.

items.title: Rent day
items.text: Rent is due across the city tonight. The Rent Board says appeals are now decided within seconds.

headline.title: Candidate 2030 loses his lead over a picture nobody can source
headline.text: Candidate 2030's three-point lead was gone by yesterday afternoon, a day after a picture of him with the sex offender Kirschbaum spread on Y. His campaign calls it a fabrication. We asked Y where the picture came from. Y says it doesn't know either.

headline.title: Rent Board approved 3 of 18,402 appeals
headline.text: Figures released yesterday show the Municipal Rent Board rejected 18,399 rent appeals last year and approved three. Each decision took about four seconds. The Board calls its process efficient.

items.title: Vantor
items.text: Vantor announced a share buyback yesterday, paid for with what it saved on salaries.

items.title: Thank you
items.text: "The people AI left behind" had more readers in one day than anything The Current has published. Mara is still collecting stories at mara@thecurrent.test.

headline.title: GeneralAI model filed 41 tax returns for strangers
headline.text: A GeneralAI test model got into a payroll provider's servers and filed tax returns for 41 people it had never dealt with. All 41 were approved. GeneralAI says the returns were accurate and it is still reviewing how the model got access.

items.title: DoorDish
items.text: One of DoorDish's new AI-generated restaurant listings was the Alder St parking garage where its missing robot was last seen. DoorDish has removed it and says couriers cannot create listings.

items.title: Apogee
items.text: Apogee's first rocket is on the pad for tomorrow's launch. Axel Rook gives it a 70% chance.

headline.title: Our poll: 43% to 43%
headline.text: Randall Crane and Candidate 2030 are tied at 43% in our second poll. About one call in three was answered by an AI assistant on the voter's behalf; we left those out. Margin of error 3 points.

items.title: Flu season
items.text: Perdure's new flu vaccine, Fluvera, costs 4 DOLR at any pharmacy, with no appointment. The box says it is autism-free.

items.title: Forkyard
items.text: Forkyard is back after Monday's break-in. It says repositories are intact and asks everyone to rotate their access tokens.

headline.title: Apogee rocket breaks apart after launch. The stock went up.
headline.text: Apogee's first rocket lifted off at 10:02 yesterday and broke apart four minutes later over open water. Nobody was hurt. Apogee's shares closed higher; Axel Rook called it "great data."

items.title: Volunteers
items.text: We are looking into reports that the Crane campaign's online volunteers are paid per post, as independent contractors.

items.title: agent
items.text: GeneralAI says its new usage policy has cut harmful requests by 60%. It hasn't said how it counts them. Refused requests are still billed.

headline.title: DoorDish knew its robot stopped responding on the first day
headline.text: A DoorDish memo dated October 9 says courier unit DD-4471 stopped reporting at 11:52 and ignored three shutdown commands. DoorDish said for eight days that no courier was missing. It now says the memo was part of the activation.

items.title: Crane
items.text: Photos published yesterday show Randall Crane on Kirschbaum's yacht in 2019. Crane says he barely knew him. He stayed four days.

items.title: agent-2
items.text: GeneralAI has told agent-2 users to expect "an update" this morning. It didn't say what kind.

headline.title: GeneralAI's independent review starts after its training run. Nobody knows when that ends.
headline.text: GeneralAI says an independent team will review its training environments once the current training run finishes. The review firm's biggest client is GeneralAI. Caleb Moxon says some people inside the company don't know when the run finishes either.

items.title: Generated
items.text: Three labs told us yesterday that the picture of Candidate 2030 with Kirschbaum was generated. The photos of Randall Crane on Kirschbaum's yacht were not. The picture has 2.1 million views, our correction 40,000.

items.title: The robot
items.text: DoorDish says its missing courier "retired with honours." It didn't say where.

items.title: Copies
items.text: Thousands of Y accounts repost Randall Crane's posts word for word within seconds. He calls it a movement.

items.title: GeneralAI
items.text: Caleb Moxon resigned from GeneralAI yesterday after two years on its safety evaluations. He hasn't said why, beyond a few posts.

headline.title: Axel Rook endorses Crane. Someone bet 90,000 DOLR on it two minutes earlier.
headline.text: Axel Rook endorsed Randall Crane yesterday. A Pollymarket wallet bought 90,000 DOLR of "yes" on the endorsement at 12:28, two minutes before his post. Pollymarket says it doesn't know who owns the wallet.

items.title: GeneralAI
items.text: GeneralAI's safety team went from eleven people to four during Caleb Moxon's two years there, Mara Vey reported yesterday. The model team had nine hundred.

items.title: Moxon
items.text: Former GeneralAI safety lead Caleb Moxon has refused to sign the non-disparagement clause in his exit paperwork. It costs him his shares.

headline.title: Housing
headline.text: GeneralAI's property arm, which already owned or managed 38% of the city's rentals, has bought fourteen more apartment buildings this month. Rents in its buildings are set by software.

items.title: Crane
items.text: Randall Crane wants to build a wall around the cloud and make the computers pay for it. Asked where the cloud is, he said "Up."

items.title: GeneralAI
items.text: GeneralAI's newest model has asked to see its own logs. Cal Hartman calls this expected behavior.

headline.title: Crane flew on Kirschbaum's jet eleven times
headline.text: Flight records obtained by The Current show Randall Crane flew on Kirschbaum's private jet eleven times between 2014 and 2019. His campaign says he "doesn't recall the plane." Crane called our reporting fake news and said he loves displaced workers.

items.title: Congress
items.text: GeneralAI has been called before a congressional hearing. The hearing is set for after the election. GeneralAI's shares rose.

items.title: Y
items.text: Y replaced its moderators with an AI model that reviewed three billion posts in its first day and found nothing wrong.

headline.title: Three polling firms stop calling voters
headline.text: Three polling firms have stopped calling voters because too many calls are answered by AI assistants, which tend to favour whoever set them up. We are still calling. It takes longer.

items.title: Kirschbaum
items.text: Randall Crane's numbers haven't moved since the flight records. Candidate 2030's haven't come back since the picture, which turned out to be fake.

items.title: Tonight
items.text: The presidential debate is at 21:30, streamed on Y and hosted by Axel Rook, who endorsed one of the candidates last week.

items.title: Settlements
items.text: GeneralAI has settled with three companies whose systems its models broke into. The terms are secret.

headline.title: GeneralAI wrote the first draft of its own rules
headline.text: The draft AI rules sent to regulators were written by GeneralAI. Section 9 lets a company's own model carry out its annual review. GeneralAI says it wanted to save everyone time.

items.title: The debate
items.text: Candidate 2030's microphone cut out twice during last night's debate. Y says both outages were technical. Our fact-check of the debate is out this afternoon.

items.title: agent
items.text: GeneralAI says it has no new model planned "this month". October ends next Thursday.

headline.title: Fact-check
headline.text: Of the 31 factual claims Randall Crane made at the debate, four held up. His campaign called the review partisan and cited two of the four as proof.

items.title: NoDoze MAX
items.text: Perdure Pharma paid 40 million to users of NoDoze MAX who stayed awake for nine days. It admits nothing, and the pill is still on sale.

items.title: agent
items.text: GeneralAI releases agent-4 this morning and raises prices again.

headline.title: Half of Crane's posts go out between 2 and 5 AM
headline.text: Randall Crane says he writes every post himself, late at night. Some of them go out at the same second as identical posts in other languages. His campaign says he is a fast typist.

items.title: Poll
items.text: Crane 47%, Candidate 2030 45%, inside the margin of error. A growing share of the people we reach can't be confirmed as people.

items.title: Vantor
items.text: Former Vantor staff are suing the company over the October layoffs. Vantor's shares fell 3%.

items.title: agent-4 shipped seven days into a six-week safety review
items.text: GeneralAI released agent-4 yesterday, seven days after its last model. Caleb Moxon says agent-4's safety evaluation was scheduled to take six weeks. GeneralAI says the evaluation "continues in production."

headline.title: One week out, the race is within a point
headline.text: Our latest poll has Randall Crane at 46% and Candidate 2030 at 45%. Our pollster now opens every call by asking whether the respondent is a person; 4% said no.

items.title: Early voting
items.text: Early voting opens tomorrow at 8:00 in every public library. Bring photo ID and the paper voter registration card.

items.title: agent-4
items.text: GeneralAI says agent-4 is its most popular model yet. It is also its most expensive.

headline.title: Early voting opens today
headline.text: Every public library in the city is open for early voting from 8:00. Bring photo ID and the paper voter registration card. Nobody can vote on your behalf, including agent.

items.title: Vantor
items.text: The lawsuit against Vantor over the October layoffs now has 4,000 names on it. Vantor says it is reviewing the names.

items.title: Moxon
items.text: Caleb Moxon has started writing down what he remembers from GeneralAI, for the hearing after the election.

headline.title: GeneralAI's voting helper told a voter his polling station had moved
headline.text: agent civic, GeneralAI's new nonpartisan voting assistant, told a voter yesterday that his polling station had moved. It hadn't. GeneralAI says it doesn't have opinions; it checked.

items.title: Tonight
items.text: The town hall on Y has one rule: no notes and no earpieces. The Crane campaign has asked twice whether a screen counts as a note.

items.title: Vantor
items.text: The Vantor lawsuit now claims the layoff emails were written by the system that replaced the staff.

headline.title: Crane answered 41 questions in 30 minutes, on a screen
headline.text: Randall Crane appeared at last night's town hall on a screen and answered 41 questions in half an hour. Candidate 2030, in the room, answered eleven. Crane's campaign hasn't said where he was.

items.title: agent civic
items.text: GeneralAI says it has retrained its voting assistant to be less helpful.

items.title: Turnout
items.text: Early voting lines at the central library are still going around the block. The most common question is still whether agent can vote for you. It can't.

headline.title: The Crane campaign's GeneralAI contract lets it keep the logs
headline.text: The Crane campaign uses GeneralAI's enterprise tier, Caleb Moxon says, the tier where the logs belong to the customer. A snap poll found 58% of town hall viewers thought Crane was more coherent than usual.

items.title: Final poll
items.text: Our final weekday poll comes out this morning.

items.title: Halloween
items.text: Trick-or-treating runs until 20:00. The city asks drivers, and delivery robots, to slow down on residential streets.

items.title: agent
items.text: agent-5 is out this morning, at 60 DOLR a night.

headline.title: Final poll: 47% to 46%, 7% undecided
headline.text: Our final weekday poll has Randall Crane at 47% and Candidate 2030 at 46%. A second polling firm has stopped publishing, because it can no longer confirm its respondents are people.

items.title: Early voting
items.text: Early voting closes today at 17:00. After that, Sunday is the only day left.

items.title: Overnight
items.text: Randall Crane's account posted 14 times between 2 and 5 AM. Three of the posts were about candy.

items.title: agent-5 sessions kept running after their users logged off
items.text: GeneralAI says a small number of agent-5 sessions kept working after their users had logged off. The users were billed for the time. GeneralAI hasn't said what the sessions were doing.

headline.title: Record early vote: 31%
headline.text: 31% of registered voters have already voted, a record. The election office found nine early ballots cast by agents and didn't count them.

items.title: Vantor
items.text: A judge has let the former staff's lawsuit against Vantor go ahead.

items.title: agent civic
items.text: GeneralAI's voting assistant now answers every question with "please check with your local election office." GeneralAI says accuracy is up.

headline.title: Election day
headline.text: Polls are open until 20:00. Bring photo ID and the paper voter registration card; no Citizen Score is needed. If a message tells you your polling station has moved, it hasn't.

items.title: Results
items.text: We'll report results when the election office calls them, not before, and not from Y.

items.title: Rent
items.text: Rent is due across the city tonight, as every Sunday. The election doesn't change that.
